attractions.name: Kargah Buddha
attractions.description: A large Buddha figure carved into a rock face, dating back to the 7th century, reflecting the region's Buddhist past.

attractions.name: Hunza Valley (day trip)
attractions.description: One of Pakistan's most famous mountain valleys, with dramatic peaks, ancient forts, and terraced orchards, reachable from Gilgit.
attractions.location_text: ~2-3 hours from Gilgit via the Karakoram Highway

attractions.name: Gilgit Bazaar
attractions.description: The main market area of Gilgit, known for dry fruits, local handicrafts, and gemstones.

attractions.name: Naltar Valley
attractions.description: A remote alpine valley near Gilgit known for colorful lakes, pine forests, and a small ski resort.

food_places.name: Dry fruit and apricot stalls

transportation.notes: Scenic flight past Nanga Parbat, but frequently subject to weather cancellations
Long but extremely scenic overland route along the Karakoram Highway
Scenic drive, hire a local car or shared van

weather_info.climate_type: Cold semi-arid mountain climate, with large temperature swings between summer and winter
weather_info.best_time_to_visit: May to October (mountain roads most reliably open)
weather_info.avoid_months: December to February (very cold, roads can be affected by snow)

seasonal_notes.avg_condition: Cold, often below freezing, especially at night
Mild and pleasant, 20-30°C during the day, cool at night
Generally clear and scenic, good for photography

travel_tips.tip: Flights from Islamabad to Gilgit are the fastest option but frequently get cancelled due to weather -- always have the Karakoram Highway route as a backup plan.
Shared vans (Coasters) and hired cars are the main way to reach Hunza and other nearby valleys from Gilgit.
Check road conditions along the Karakoram Highway before traveling, as landslides can occasionally cause temporary closures, especially after heavy rain.
Plan flexible travel dates in this region since weather can delay both flights and, occasionally, road travel.

history.founded: An ancient settlement along historic Silk Road trade routes, with a history spanning over a thousand years
history.city_history: Gilgit was a key stop on trade routes connecting South Asia, Central Asia, and China, and was ruled by various local dynasties before coming under British political influence in the 19th century. It has served as the main administrative and gateway city for the Gilgit-Baltistan region since Pakistan's independence.
history.province_history: Gilgit-Baltistan is a mountainous region in northern Pakistan, home to some of the world's highest peaks including K2. It has a distinct administrative status, having acceded to Pakistan in 1947 separately from the rest of the country, and was granted a measure of self-governance in 2009.
